description:
Scenario: stdlib stabilizes a new ErrorKind variant (this has happened repeatedly — see the io_error_more tracking issue, stabilized in tranches across 1.83 and surrounding releases).

Maintenance consequence: each stabilization either silently loses information through pkix-aia's serde label helper (current behavior — see PKIX-o3op.1), or pkix-aia must ship a patch that adds the new variant to two parallel match arms (label_for and kind_for at pkix-aia/src/lib.rs:289-344). The same patch must update the cases table in tests at lines 356-377. Three places, no compile-time check that they stay in sync.

If the design is preserved (hand-maintained table), at minimum the maintenance contract should be made explicit: a comment saying 'this table must be updated whenever stdlib stabilizes a new ErrorKind variant; the build will not catch omissions' would help. Currently the contract is implicit and the existing comments overstate the helper's coverage (see PKIX-o3op.2 and PKIX-o3op.3).

The forward-compat fallback at line 312 ('_ => "Other"' for the deserialize side via kind_for) is only half the contract. The serialize side has no such fallback — silently emitting 'Other' for an unknown variant is the bug, not the cushion.

Resolving PKIX-o3op.1 by option (b) (format!("{kind:?}") in serialize) eliminates this maintenance tax entirely. Resolving it by option (a) (extending the table) accepts the recurring tax.

This is the architectural decision worth recording: do future-stdlib labels round-trip by construction, or by ongoing maintenance?
title: label_for table is a recurring maintenance tax across stdlib releases
